features.text: Patient has a hyperextension injury of the right index finger sustained during a motor vehicle accident in March of this year.
Patient has a history of a reaction to dexamethasone, which causes his heart to race.

Patient had an MRI of the right index finger on 4/24/2021, which showed focal soft tissue swelling over the right index MCP joint, partial-thickness tear of the right FDS, and fluid consistent with tenosynovitis around the FDP and FDS tendons.
Patient's x-rays of the right hand show no bony abnormalities, joint congruency throughout all lesser digits on the right hand, no soft tissue shadows of concern, and no arthritis.
Patient reports that the right index finger has been painful since March, and the pain is sometimes unbearable.
Patient is unable to make a fist with the right hand.
Patient reports that the right index finger is swollen.
Patient reports that driving hurts due to the injury.
Patient has been receiving physical therapy and occupational therapy for the right index finger.
Patient was sent to get an MRI after being seen by an orthopedist.
Patient was told by a previous provider that an injection could make the tear worse.
Patient was advised not to rub the affected finger or use it excessively.
Patient is right-handed and needs the affected hand for daily activities.
Patient is an X-ray tech by occupation.
Patient does not have a history of smoking.
Patient takes a blood pressure pill as medication.
Patient has a history of a reaction to dexamethasone, which causes his heart to race.
On physical examination, the patient has bruising on the volar surface of the right index finger.
On physical examination, the patient has slightly diminished creases over the PIP of the right index finger.
On physical examination, the patient's right index finger rests in a 10-degree PIP-flexed position.
On physical examination, the patient experiences discomfort when the PIP joint is corrected.
On physical examination, the patient experiences numbness in the right index finger.
On physical examination, the patient is able to bend the tip of the right index finger, but it feels like it is tearing.
On physical examination, the patient is able to make a fist with the right hand, but it is painful.
On physical examination, the patient has a partial tear of one half of the FDS tendon of the right index finger.
On physical examination, the patient has a functional FDS tendon that goes all the way to the tip of the right index finger.
Patient has a history of receiving a methylprednisolone injection, which caused itching.
Patient has a history of occupational therapy attempts to straighten the right index finger, which resulted in pain and swelling.
Patient is concerned about being able to drive after the injection.
Patient has not scheduled therapy at the moment.
